source: round-9 reviews (r9-1 and its re-review r9-1v): every Node result class of the r9-1 generator sets c1-c10, combo and flip (2-3 cases per class), the e2e keyring PEMs and ecpriv_*.pem, and from the re-review c13 (every case that differed from Go at 1499697 plus 300 random ones), 101 c10 cases, det_flip.pem, priv_flip2.pem and kr_E.json. Some are random in Node (OpenSSL blinding over a reducible field or composite modulus); TestLivePEMKeyParsing resolves a disagreement by re-running both sides. Each text is stored as the hex of its WTF-8 bytes in reverse order (revHex), so secret scanners do not read the private-key-shaped test inputs as keys
